title: Book VIII
coreMove: Replace appearance management and complaint with the next correctable useful act.
sourcePressure: Seeming philosophical is rejected in favor of present useful action, correction without blame, dropping complaint, and using hindered plans as material.
chapterSpecificMisunderstanding: look authentic while doing the same delayed behavior

sourceAnchors.name: stop choosing to be good tomorrow
sourceAnchors.detail: Book VIII names procrastinated goodness as a moral failure: stop choosing to be good tomorrow rather than today.
sourceAnchors.phrasingHint: Tomorrow-goodness is attractive because it lets the present self keep its old permissions.

sourceAnchors.name: correct the cause or the thing itself
sourceAnchors.detail: Book VIII says fault-finding is useless when one can instead correct the cause or the thing itself.
sourceAnchors.phrasingHint: Complaint ends when the hand moves toward the cause instead of polishing the grievance.

counterintuition: what looks like control is actually surrender
the real problem is not outside you
tryThisNow: write down what you can control
examples: generic office meeting with laptop and coffee
parent-child bedtime conflict repeated across chapters

exampleOpeningDiversity.rule: no more than 2 of the 6 examples may open with the pattern 'At HH:MM, <Name> <verb>s'
exampleOpeningDiversity.requiredOpenings: at least 4 distinct opening devices across the 6 examples, drawn from: timestamp+name+action, dialogue first line, sensory detail first, second-person direct address, retrospective recognition, question-as-hook, environmental detail before any human
exampleOpeningDiversity.rationale: C8 catches Cartesian repetition of phrases but not the deeper template of 'timestamp + named protagonist + prop + decision' that makes 6 examples feel like 1 example with name swaps

exampleSpecs.audience: Sarah dealing with recurring boiler calls
exampleSpecs.stakes: residents need heat, not another group chat speech
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Sarah stops writing the complaint post and tapes the technician's access notice to every door.
exampleSpecs.firstImage: Cold air sits under the lobby doors like water.

exampleSpecs.audience: Marco facing a broken appointment system
exampleSpecs.stakes: staff keep blaming students for missed slots
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Marco replaces the confusing sign-up sheet with a numbered queue before the next rush.
exampleSpecs.firstImage: The advising hallway fills before the office lights finish warming up.

exampleSpecs.stakes: another angry recap will not fix the missing label step
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: "No lecture today," Beatrice says, then puts red allergen clips on the pass and rehearses the handoff.

exampleSpecs.audience: Hugo handling a confusing renewal form
exampleSpecs.stakes: visitors keep making the same mistake because the form invites it
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: You watch Hugo cross out one misleading line on the sample form before blaming the next visitor.
exampleSpecs.firstImage: You see the same question mark penciled beside the same line.

exampleSpecs.stakes: drivers are blamed for a pickup shelf nobody can read
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: It took Ada four late crowns to label the shelf instead of accusing the courier.
exampleSpecs.firstImage: It took Ada four late crowns to notice the shelf had no morning side.

exampleSpecs.audience: Ryan discovering damaged returns from one display
exampleSpecs.stakes: fault-finding at staff would hide the bad shelf angle
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: What if the complaint is pointing to carpentry, not character?
exampleSpecs.firstImage: Ryan moves the display six inches, then watches returns stop for a week.

rhythmVariety.deepReadParagraphLengthMix: at least one paragraph 3 sentences or shorter, at least one paragraph 5+ sentences, at least one one-sentence punch line
rhythmVariety.fullReadInterludeRequirement: at least one paragraph that breaks the scene-then-rule rhythm: a question to the reader, a research aside, a direct second-person passage, or a brief historical reference
rhythmVariety.forbiddenRhythm: every paragraph following the pattern 'concrete anchor sentence -> abstract rule sentence -> elaboration sentence'

skillTargets: use hindrance without complaint or passivity

tryThisNowSpec: Pick one complaint you have repeated twice and correct the smallest cause you can touch before explaining it again.
